meta.source: This page’s own dataset is _data/SOURCES.json (the source registry) and _data/catalog.json (the generated inventory of build scripts), joined to five shipped page files: wages for the concentration reading and the industry-code arithmetic, occupations for the education-boundary example, peers for the disclosure rates, revisions for how far these series move after publication, and laborshed for the measured gap.
meta.row: One row of the register is one source: its endpoint, the exact filter values applied to it, whether it needs a key, and every page here that rests on it.
meta.definition: How you get it is DERIVED from the endpoint’s shape, not declared in the registry, and the four tests run IN THIS ORDER: no endpoint at all is an internal record; then a URL ending in a file extension is a bulk download; then a URL with an api path segment is an API request; then a URL ending in a directory is a bulk download; and anything left is a portal query. The order is printed because it decides the answer rather than describing it: two of these endpoints end in a directory AND carry an api segment, and reading the tests in a different order relabels them. The rule is on the page so a reader can disagree with a label rather than inherit it.
meta.why: The register lists only the sources behind the analyses published in this repository. The internal series has more pages and more sources, and their absence is stated rather than left to be discovered.
meta.scope: This page hands over method, not data. It does not republish any source, and following it will not give you these numbers: it will give you the same numbers for your own region, which is the point.
meta.not: A licence and a set of terms are different things and the register keeps them apart. Two sources state a LICENCE that conditions use: O*NET is CC BY 4.0 and IPEDS reaches this site through the Urban Institute’s portal under ODC-By 1.0. Both require attribution, and both credits are printed in this page’s footer with a link to the licence, because describing a licence is not complying with one. The federal statistical series state TERMS instead, which is public domain with a citation request, and those are quoted on each entry with the agency page they come from, rather than left as an implication that no term exists.
meta.caution: Two of the fourteen sources have no endpoint and no script. They are internal records, the published file is the artifact, and nothing on this site can make them fetchable.

sources.name: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
sources.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm
sources.is: A census, not a survey. It counts every job covered by unemployment insurance, from returns employers already have to file, so it carries no sampling error and no margin of error to report.
sources.good: Jobs, establishment counts and average weekly wages, by county and by industry code, quarterly and as annual averages, back to 1990.
sources.cannot: It cannot see the self-employed, most farm labour, or anyone outside the insurance system, and it withholds any cell where too few employers would be identifiable. Its wage is an average per covered job: not a salary, not per person, and it moves with hours and occupational mix as well as with pay.
filters: 10 (all industries), 31-33 (manufacturing), 325 (chemical manufacturing), 3252 (resin, synthetic rubber and fibers), 3255 (paint, coating and adhesive), 326 (plastics and rubber products), 3261 (plastics products), 3262 (rubber products)

own_code 5 (private) carries every industry row; own_code 0 (total, all ownerships) exists only on industry 10. Those are not two interchangeable choices: an industry row at own_code 0 does not exist to be picked.

county area file: agglvl_code 70 is the all-ownership county total, 71 the county total by ownership, 74 NAICS sector, 75 NAICS 3-digit, 76 NAICS 4-digit, 77 5-digit, 78 6-digit. The US000 file uses 10, 11, 15, 16 and 18 for the same rungs. agglvl 50 to 58 are STATE levels and appear in no county file: 55 is three-digit, 56 four-digit, 57 five-digit and 58 six-digit.

county FIPS (the federal numeric code that identifies each county). The page’s own footprint, PIC-12, is 39007 Ashtabula, 39035 Cuyahoga, 39055 Geauga, 39085 Lake, 39093 Lorain, 39099 Mahoning, 39103 Medina, 39133 Portage, 39151 Stark, 39153 Summit, 39155 Trumbull, 39169 Wayne. The chain page uses a separate 14-county company-register boundary, documented in its data. The legacy NEO14 constant in footprints.py is a different county set and must not be substituted for that boundary.

the same census sliced the other way, one file per NAICS across every area, at https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/{year}/a/industry/{naics}.csv. The disclosure rates published on the sources page are the 2024 annual file for 326, own_code 5: county rows are agglvl 75, metropolitan rows agglvl 45, state rows agglvl 55.

This source is on data.bls.gov, which serves a scripted request with any User-Agent or none. The 403 is on www.bls.gov, which the two OEWS (the Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics survey) files use, and the warning is filed on those rather than here.
PIC’s own measurement register is 3252 + 3255 + 326. NAICS 325 is context, not cluster: it contains pharmaceuticals and agricultural chemicals.

fetch_provenance.py re-uses this source for one pull: 2016 annual, area 39000 which is the STATE of Ohio and not a county, own_code 5, industry 326+32521+325991 at agglvl 55/57/58, which are the state 3-, 5- and 6-digit levels. Those three agglvl codes belong to that state pull alone and return nothing from a county file.
The held 2024 private NAICS 326 state slice contains all 50 states plus Puerto Rico (72000); DC (11000) is absent. Membership is asserted by FIPS identities, not inferred from a count of 51.

The current real-wage comparison uses private NAICS 326 annual-average wages and employment for 2024, with metro rows at agglvl 45. QCEW adopted OMB bulletin 23-01 (2023-07-21) in 2024. Cleveland changes from C1746 through 2023 to C1741 in 2024 and adds Ashtabula; continuing a code does not establish constant boundaries. Detailed-industry metro publication ended beginning Q3 2025. Source notices: https://www.bls.gov/cew/notices/2024/new-metropolitan-statistical-area-delineations-for-2024.htm and https://www.bls.gov/cew/notices/2025/change-in-the-presentation-of-metropolitan-statistical-area-data-in-qcew.htm

The wages page includes broad chemical manufacturing 325 and plastics/rubber 326, plus their separately disclosed parts. Broad 325 includes pharmaceuticals and agricultural chemicals. The complete non-overlapping group comparison weights county/group-average pay ratios by jobs; it is not an individual wage distribution. Private manufacturing 31-33 is a separate comparator; industry 10 all-ownership county pay is the local all-jobs benchmark.

own_code 5; annual qtr a; NAICS 326; years 2015-2025. Fixed PIC-12 county set, Ohio 39000, US000 and all five Ohio-bordering states 18000/21000/26000/42000/54000. annual_avg_emplvl and annual_avg_estabs are annual averages, not same-establishment panel records. Manufacturing 31-33 is separately labelled PIC-12 context. cluster-health/derive_health.py --workplaces-only transforms held by-area/by-industry extracts; source hashes and overlap checks are in cluster-health/data/workplaces.json. This is a held-snapshot comparison, not a new bulk upstream revision audit.

County and by-industry extracts are acquired separately. The published geography/workplace changes were rederived from held QCEW inputs; a current API request can return a different revision. Public derived files record the input hashes and dated scope.

sources.name: USAspending federal contract and grant obligations
sources.terms: Public domain federal spending data. USAspending states no additional licence.
sources.is: The Treasury’s public record of federal awards: contracts, grants and other obligations, filed by the agency that made them.
sources.good: How much federal money is obligated to work performed in a place, cut by industry code and fiscal year.
sources.cannot: An obligation is money legally committed, not cash spent, and place of performance is a field the award reports rather than an observation of where the work happened. An industry-code filter cannot see a university or a research institute, which file under entirely different codes. It also cannot tell you a programme ceiling: an award record carries what is obligated, a press release usually quotes a multi-year maximum, and this site once printed the two for the same award on two pages, $160M against $14,999,983, before a reader found them side by side.
filters: POST with a JSON body, and the {category} path segment is required: naics and county are the two this site asks for. The endpoint without a category returns 404 to GET and to POST alike, which is what a reader who copies the stem alone will meet.

Not sent to the category API. Acquire all pages for a fiscal year/category, then retain 325* and 326* client-side. These include chemical and plastics/rubber manufacturing; university/research grants are excluded from the prime-contract manufacturing view by the award-type and industry filters.

limit=100, starting page=1; validate page_metadata.page, hasNext and next through a terminal hasNext=false,next=null. Malformed, missing, duplicate or non-finite rows fail. Keep signed obligations, including de-obligations, and apply the industry filter only after exhaustion.
place of performance, a reported field on the award rather than an observation of where work happened
Obligations are money legally committed, not cash spent.

Primary NAICS rows and the same-basis all-industry contracting comparator use award_type_codes A, B, C, D (prime contracts). Separately labelled all-type county context has no award-type filter and must never be used as the contracting denominator.
spending_level=transactions; one October 1-September 30 window per fiscal year FY2019-FY2026. FY2019-FY2025 are completed years; FY2026 is a partial snapshot excluded from the annual average.

The all-type context separately queries contracts, indefinite-delivery vehicles (IDV), grants, loans, direct payments and other assistance. Their signed sum can differ from a separately queried live total; retain and disclose the unallocated remainder rather than asserting exact reconciliation.

Complete category acquisition dated 2026-09-08; request/response hashes and terminal pagination receipts identify the pull. derive_federal.py produces the public fiscal-year file; derive_rest.py delegates that transformation. A future request may revise obligations.

sources.name: IPEDS Completions, via the Urban Institute Education Data API, with three years read from NCES directly
sources.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, served by the Urban Institute
sources.attribution: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) Completions, via Education Data Portal v. 0.26.1, Urban Institute, accessed 18 August 2026, https://educationdata.urban.org/documentation/, made available under the ODC (Open Data Commons) Attribution License.
sources.terms: The underlying IPEDS collection is a public-domain federal series, but the route this site uses is not the federal one. Everything served through the Urban Institute’s Education Data Portal is licensed to the user under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By) v1.0, which REQUIRES attribution and a citation naming the portal version and the access date: https://educationdata.urban.org/documentation/. Portal version 0.26.1 was released 2026-08-05 and was current at this site’s access date of 2026-08-18.
sources.is: The federal record of every degree and certificate conferred by every institution that takes federal student aid, filed by six-digit programme code.
sources.good: Counting the graduates of named programmes at named institutions, year by year, against the same programmes nationally.
sources.cannot: It counts people finishing a programme, never people hired and never people who stayed in the region. A programme code returning zero at every institution in every year is far more likely to be a bad code than a real absence of graduates.
filters: 143201 (polymer/plastics engineering), 400507 (polymer chemistry), 150607 (plastics and polymer engineering technology)

141801 (materials engineering), 400510 (materials chemistry), 401001 (materials science), 141901 (mechanical engineering), 140701 (chemical engineering), 400501 (chemistry general), 151701 (energy systems technology)
1 only, so a double major is counted once
race=99 and sex=99 are the total rows; race=8 is nonresident alien. The two partitions are aggregated separately and never crossed; this endpoint does not offer the cross-tab at CIP-6.

the same codes with no state filter, restricted to codes the footprint itself confers as a programme (which excludes 150607), since PIC-12’s entire history in it is two awards from one community college in one year

Two earlier code entries did not exist and silently returned zero: 140320 (a transposition of 143201) and 143101 (materials science is in the 40 series, not 14). A core code returning zero across every year and institution is evidence of a bad code, not of no graduates.
fetch_ipeds_cip.py adds institution × CIP × year (used by talent and occupations)

The mirror’s year is the FALL of the academic year, so its 2023 is the NCES C2024_A file. That convention held through 2019 and again at 2023; in between, its 2020, 2021 and 2022 each served the collection year before the one they name, and C2023_A was served under no label at all. Those three years are therefore taken from the NCES completions files (https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/data/C{year}_A.zip, no key), by fetch_ipeds_nces.py; the correction table and its re-check are in _data/build/ipeds_mirror_fix.py. Degrees only: the recovered year also carries two postbaccalaureate certificates, which no other year of the series counts.

sources.name: BLS CPI-U, all items, U.S. city average
sources.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm
sources.is: BLS monthly CPI-U, all items, U.S. city average, not seasonally adjusted; annual means provide a common purchasing-power basis.
sources.good: Restating dollars from different years on one stated price basis.
sources.cannot: Calendar-year consumer prices only approximate fiscal-year prices and industrial input costs. The 2025 mean uses eleven published months because October is missing; FY2026 carries the 2025 index as an approximation.
filters: CUUR0000SA0, monthly not-seasonally-adjusted all-items CPI-U, U.S. city average; years 2019-2025.

Exclude M13 summary rows and unavailable observations, then average the published monthly values and round to three decimals. Years 2019-2024 contain twelve months; 2025 contains eleven, with October unavailable, giving 321.943. Missing October is not imputed.

Constant 2025 dollars: multiply signed nominal obligations by 2025 CPI / fiscal-year-labelled calendar CPI. Calendar-year prices approximate fiscal-year prices; FY2026 carries the 2025 index as an explicit approximation.
BLS monthly response acquired 2026-09-08; response hash and annual monthly membership are carried in federal-money/data/federal.json cpi_observations. Future CPI revisions may change the result.

fetch_federal_cpi.py writes monthly response plus annual means into an explicit fresh output directory; derive_federal.py consumes these verified observations. The unrelated older long-history CPI cache is not overwritten.

sources.name: FRED producer price and commodity series
sources.agency: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.is: The St Louis Fed’s distribution of federal price series: producer price indexes and commodity spot prices, served from one API under one key.
sources.good: Following what a feedstock, a resin or a finished good costs over time, on a common base you choose.
sources.cannot: Index levels are not dollars, and producer prices are not consumer prices. Nothing arrives deflated, so a rise you have not divided by a price index is a cash figure and needs saying so.
filters: WPU072 (PPI rubber and plastic products), WPU066 (PPI plastics resins and materials), WPU06 (PPI industrial chemicals), PCU326326 (PPI plastics and rubber products manufacturing), PCU325211325211 (PPI plastics material and resin manufacturing), WTISPLC (WTI crude oil spot)
Producer price indexes, not consumer prices. Index levels, not dollars.
fetch_rest.py FIRST, then fetch_chain_prices.py. The second appends the feedstock and resin links to fred.json; running fetch_rest.py after it overwrites the file and silently drops them.

sources.name: IPEDS completions by 6-digit CIP, held polymer-program census, 1991-2023
sources.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, via the Urban Institute Education Data API
sources.is: Degree and certificate completions by six-digit programme code, 1991 to 2023, for the three polymer codes.
sources.good: Counting what American colleges actually conferred under a polymer heading, year by year, on one consistent national definition.
sources.cannot: It sees only the programmes a college chose to report under a polymer code. Soft-matter teaching filed under chemistry, physics or materials is invisible to it, and at least five institutions are confirmed to teach the subject while appearing here as nothing. A year with no completions is a filing gap, never a closure. 2024 returns HTTP 500 from the API and is probed on every build, so every recent figure is a floor.
filters: 14.3201 Polymer/Plastics Engineering; 40.0507 Polymer Chemistry; 15.0607 Plastics and Polymer Engineering Technology

Held 1991-2023 record from the 2026-08-21 census build. Quarantine mirror year 2020, which repeats 2019. The mirror year/collection mismatch and missing collection limit continuity; a derivation does not probe current API availability.
first majors only from 2000; the distinction does not exist before 2000 and filtering earlier years on it silently returns zero rows
certificate levels canonicalised across the 2020 IPEDS renumbering (1->31, 2/3->32, 5/6->33) before any counting

derive_programs.py transforms a held SQLite program census and companion extracts; it does not reacquire the national record. Configure PROGRAMS_DB to the held database. The public derived file is shipped; the full source database is not included in this repository.

One program record is institution identifier x CIP x award level. Substantive: more than 10 recorded lifetime completions. Active: positive completion in the final reported year 2023. Small: at most 10. Brief: inclusive first-to-last reported calendar-year span at most 5, not the number of positive years. Small-and-brief means both.

Selected-code reporting is not institutional survival, teaching closure, a failed start or a historical first. Missing years can change both threshold membership and denominators; the snapshot shares are not failure probabilities or guaranteed bounds on a complete census.
Snapshot reconciliation against held inputs is distinct from live acquisition. The completed update rechecked public program aggregates against the held census without a new national API pull.

sources.name: NSF Awards API
sources.is: The National Science Foundation’s own record of what it awarded, to whom, and when.
sources.good: Establishing that a specific federal award exists, its size and its dates, from the awarding agency rather than from a press release.
sources.cannot: The PRIME RECIPIENT is not the lead institution of the work, and reading it as such is the single error this project has made most often. Collaborative work is frequently issued as separate awards to each institution, so one award naming one university is not evidence that the other was uninvolved.
filters: Collaboration analyses: every award to the two selected universities since 2012-01-01. The federal-money exclusion note instead retrieves two named awards by exact identifier, as described separately below.
two ways: one award naming investigators at both institutions by email domain, and NSF’s ‘Collaborative Research’ mechanism, which issues a separate award per institution under an identical title

Only awards NSF itself labels ‘Collaborative Research’ are counted as joint. Matching on shared title alone booked ‘Graduate Research Fellowship Program’: an institutional block grant every university receives separately, as a $1.1M joint project.

Exact award IDs 2532460 and 2330145, fetched from https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/{id}.json by fetch_federal_research.py. Preserve estimated award amount and obligated amount as different fields; these research awards illustrate exclusions from the prime-contract North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) scope, not additions to its totals.

sources.name: Ohio LMI long-term employment projections, 2022–2032
sources.agency: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Bureau of Labor Market Information
sources.is: Ohio’s own long-term employment projections, published as spreadsheets by region and by occupation rather than through any API.
sources.good: A state agency’s view of where an industry and its occupations are headed inside Ohio, at a geography federal files do not offer.
sources.cannot: A projection is a modelled path with no confidence band, and it historically under-calls turning points. Two of this site’s three register codes are published only inside wider bundles, so the register cannot be rebuilt from it.
filters: JobsOhio Northeast (18 counties, superset of PIC-12) and the four MSAs; Ashtabula and Wayne appear only in region and state figures
one industry or one SOC (the Standard Occupational Classification, the federal job-title code) occupation × geography: 2022 base, 2032 projected, change, percent, annual openings split, median wage
a modelled path with no confidence band; historically under-calls turning points
3252 is published only inside bundle 3250A1 and 3255 only inside 3250A2; only 326/3261/3262 are clean
ohiolmi.com returns 403 to a scripted request, browser User-Agent or not, so this one is a manual download: open the directory in a browser and save the spreadsheet. Verified 2026-08-29.

sources.name: OpenAlex works and institutions
sources.is: An open bibliographic index of published work and the institutions attached to it.
sources.good: Seeing who a region’s researchers publish with, and where the work travels.
sources.cannot: Attribution rests on a convention: credit goes to the corresponding author, which is where a lab is, not necessarily where the work was done. Affiliation strings are noisy enough that a public library appeared as a leading polymer partner until it was quarantined by hand. Coverage favours indexed venues, so silence is not absence of work.
filters: I110152177 (University of Akron), I58956616 (Case Western Reserve University)
topics.subfield.id:2507, ‘Polymers and Plastics’. A CLASSIFICATION, not a keyword.
subfield 2502 ‘Biomaterials’, counted separately and never merged in
subfield ids confirmed against s3://openalex/data/jsonl/subfields, not inferred from documentation

An earlier bound matched the full-text word ‘polymer’ and returned 4,037 works, four of whose five largest partners were hospitals. The classification returns 1,448. Author position uses is_corresponding, not first author, because in this field the first author is normally the graduate student.

fetch_openalex.py hits this same endpoint but is still on the old keyword bound and returns the superseded 4,037 figure. No published page reads its output, so it is left out rather than handing a reader a script that reproduces the wrong number. Audited 2026-08-17.

sources.name: PIC public record, dated milestones
sources.is: A hand-compiled register of dated public milestones, merged from operational reports, funding files and primary press, with a source for every date.
sources.good: Placing a designation, an award or an opening on a timeline that someone else can check event by event.
sources.cannot: There is no endpoint and no script: it can be re-read but not re-fetched. Only events recorded as public appear, so the record of which dates slipped is deliberately absent from it.
filters: Merged from eight internal and public record sets: operational status reports, funding and award files, verified deck facts, and primary-press dates from the quote bank. 487 raw rows reduced to 104 dated events.
Only events recorded as PUBLIC appear. Internal operational milestones, and the record of which dates slipped, are deliberately excluded; this is the public record, not the project’s whole history.
18 of the 104 are future milestones and are drawn hollow, so a plan never reads as a fact.

Hand-compiled from documents rather than fetched from an API. Every event carries its own date and organisation; there is no script that regenerates this file, and pretending otherwise would be the opposite of what this registry is for.

sources.name: BEA Regional Price Parities, metropolitan archive (MARPP)
sources.terms: Public domain. BEA publishes citation guidelines: https://www.bea.gov/help/guidelines-for-citing-bea
sources.is: A price level rather than a price: an index with the national average set to 100, saying what a fixed basket costs in one metropolitan area against another.
sources.good: Turning a nominal wage into what it actually buys where it is earned.
sources.cannot: It is published for metropolitan areas, whose coverage differs from a county footprint. Metros overlapping PIC-12 cannot be added into its total: Canton-Massillon includes Carroll outside PIC-12, while Wayne belongs to the Wooster micropolitan area.
filters: Official metropolitan price-parity archive (MARPP), supplied as a zip archive; MARPP_MSA_2008_2024.csv and MARPP__Footnotes.html from the 2026-02-19 release.
2024 column; LineCode 1 (all items); GeoName contains Metropolitan Statistical Area. LineCode 3 (housing rents) is contextual data, not the all-items wage deflator.
US average price level = 100. Adjusted weekly pay is the QCEW industry-average weekly wage divided by RPP / 100.

Both 2024 QCEW and the archive footnote use OMB bulletin 23-01, dated 2023-07-21. Match metro identifiers only after establishing that common definition. These are metro comparisons, not a PIC-12 county aggregate.

Private NAICS 326 in 2024: 155 disclosed QCEW metro rows match BEA; 227 QCEW rows are explicitly suppressed, zero otherwise unmatched. Rank comparison uses the 29 matched metros with at least 2,000 jobs. Akron and Cleveland are included; record absence alone is not classified as suppression.

python _data/build/fetch_rpp.py --output-dir <fresh-cache>; optional --archive <held-MARPP.zip> extracts an already acquired official zip archive. The destination must be new. Exact CSV, footnotes and receipt are retained; no API key is needed.

derive_realwage.py requires --rpp-csv, --rpp-footnotes and --rpp-receipt, plus --qcew-receipt and --qcew-adoption-notice for the annotated QCEW source. It verifies actual input bytes and compares the parsed BEA defining statement with the QCEW adoption. Local classification also requires --metro-counties and --metro-counties-receipt, derived from Census OMB 23-01 county delineations: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/metro-micro/geographies/reference-files/2023/delineation-files/list1_2023.xlsx. Every intersecting area has an explicit disposition. The QCEW notice is a preserved web-tool rendering; its hash verifies custody, not agency accuracy. The annotation preserves its parent hash and data rows. The old keyed RPP cache is not this input. fetch_bea.py acquires county GDP (CAGDP2), a different measure.

Archive acquired 2026-09-08; release 2026-02-19, new 2024 and revised 2008-2023 estimates. Archive SHA256 5dbf2e6ac2af222cc9abc205586c9b480344d89392752eb689c3ec823a34c83e. Exact extract hashes appear in realwage/data/realwage.json source_receipts; future downloads may revise.

sources.name: Census County Business Patterns
sources.is: A yearly Census count of business ESTABLISHMENTS, meaning physical sites. A firm with three plants appears three times.
sources.good: Comparing chemical manufacturing and plastics/rubber establishments and their disclosed employment across counties using the same industry codes.
sources.cannot: It cannot tell you what a site actually makes beyond its industry code, it suppresses any cell small enough to identify an employer, and it counts a different thing from PIC’s own register: Census counts sites, PIC classifies company records. Dividing those records by establishments does not measure how completely PIC has identified a county’s businesses.
filters: ESTABLISHMENTS: one physical site, not one company. A firm with three plants is three establishments.

The page compares chemical manufacturing (325) and plastics/rubber products (326). These broad groups are not the narrower PIC industry register. Census establishments and PIC company records are different units; their quotient is not a coverage rate.

The company-register 14-county boundary: 39007 Ashtabula, 39029 Columbiana, 39035 Cuyahoga, 39055 Geauga, 39085 Lake, 39093 Lorain, 39099 Mahoning, 39103 Medina, 39133 Portage, 39151 Stark, 39153 Summit, 39155 Trumbull, 39157 Tuscarawas, 39169 Wayne. This contains PIC-12 plus Columbiana and Tuscarawas; it differs from the legacy NEO14 constant in footprints.py.

County Business Patterns (CBP), 2023; get NAME,ESTAB,EMP (area name, establishments, employees); for county:*; in state:39; NAICS2017=325 and NAICS2017=326 in separate requests, then select the fourteen county FIPS. Both responses were acquired on 2026-09-11 and retained with SHA256 receipts.

repair_chain.py reads the two cached raw responses without a network call. fetch_cbp.py is a separate size-class investigation using PIC-12 and narrower industry codes; it does not produce this page’s Census comparison.

sources.name: NEO Polymer Wins register, heritage and discoveries collections
sources.agency: Polymer Industry Cluster (internal register; only PROVEN rows and public sources travel)
sources.is: An internal register of what the region invented and what changed its capacity, of which only the rows its own index marks PROVEN are published.
sources.good: Naming a first, or a capability, with a public source attached to it.
sources.cannot: The register is internal and its builder cannot be run from a public clone, so the shipped file is the artifact rather than a reproducible output. Every published row carries its own public sources instead.
filters: Only rows the register’s INDEX labels PROVEN are emitted; the 5 CLAIMED rows are withheld as id + label + year only, with no wording.
heritage (what changed the region’s capacity) and discoveries (what was first understood here). The shipped, licensed, living and pic-era collections are a different tense and are not on this page.
Only http(s) URLs and bibliographic lines travel; vault-path source references are stripped at build and counted (3).
Every emitted sentence is checked against the register’s own do-not-say list; a hit fails the build.
Four different measures exist in the sources and none is printed, which is the register’s standing rule.

The register is internal; the builder (PIC-decks/tools/build-heritage-web.py) cannot be re-run from a public clone. The emitted data/heritage.json IS the published artifact, like the operating record; every row carries its public source URLs so each can be checked by hand.

sources.name: IPEDS snapshots for six peer technician trades
sources.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, via the Urban Institute Education Data API
sources.is: The identical pull run against six neighbouring technician programme codes, as a control.
sources.good: Telling whether something that happened to polymer programmes happened to comparable technical programmes too.
sources.cannot: It is a comparison set, not a second measurement of the cluster, and it inherits every blindness of the polymer census: both see reporting choices rather than teaching.
filters: 48.0508 Welding; 48.0501 Machine Tool; 15.0613 Manufacturing Eng Tech; 47.0303 Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance; 15.0303 Electrical/Electronic Eng Tech; 15.0805 Mechanical Eng Tech

Same selected years and award-level canonicalisation as the polymer census. Substantive: >10 lifetime completions; active: a reported completion in 2023. Small: <=10; brief: inclusive first-to-last reporting span <=5; small-and-brief: both.

The 2023 active-share comparison reads a held control_cips.json snapshot through derive_programs.py. The separate base-rate control was acquired by fetch_ipeds_control_baserate.py. A later live acquisition and a held census are not the same source vintage.

The substantive reporting comparison uses 6,648 records, 3,185 active in 2023 (48%). The separate all-record base-rate snapshot uses 8,736 records; 2,051 small, 2,967 brief and 1,693 both. Its refetched substantive control was 6,685/3,178, rounding to the same 48%; matching rounded rates does not make the counts or source dates identical.

Missing years may alter threshold membership and the denominator on each side. Shared mirror gaps do not guarantee that error cancels in a ratio. These are descriptive reporting shares, not failure probabilities.

sources.name: IPEDS institutional directory (coordinates and identity)
sources.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, via the Urban Institute Education Data API
sources.is: The federal directory of institutions: who they are, and since 2009 where they are.
sources.good: Placing a college on a map and confirming its identity across years.
sources.cannot: The coordinate fields begin in 2009, so anything that stopped filing before then has no location and is placed by hand at its city centre. More importantly: a directory year omits institutions that were already gone, and absence from it is not evidence of closure. Several institutions missing from a recent year are open and teaching.
filters: per-unitid, year 2023 with fallback to the institution’s last active year

A directory year can omit an institution that stopped reporting under that identifier; absence is not proof of closure. Coordinate fields begin in 2009. Seven records without usable coordinates were placed at documented city centroids, with per-record provenance.
points and basemap pre-projected at build time into the us-atlas AlbersUSA frame (975x610, scale 1300, translate 487.5/305): NOT d3 defaults
Totals count federal institution identifiers, which can change through reorganizations or recoding. Reporting in 2023 is a dated completion measure, not a current catalogue of teaching.

sources.name: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics, LODES8
sources.terms: Public domain. The Census Bureau asks to be cited as the source of the original data: https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html
sources.is: A count of JOBS, each one linking the census block where the job is to the block where its holder’s address is on file. LODES8 is the current vintage and JT00 is the segment meaning all jobs in all sectors.
sources.good: Where the people who work in a place live, and the reciprocal: where the people who live in a place work.
sources.cannot: It is not a commute. Nothing in it counts a trip, and the home end is a residence on file rather than evidence that anyone travelled. Its three broad industry groups cannot isolate polymer industries. The page uses all-job totals for the whole economy.
filters: JT00 all jobs, using S000 all-industry totals. LODES origin-destination has three broad industry groups, but cannot isolate polymer industries.
main (both ends in state) plus aux (work in state, home out of state). Omitting aux makes the region look artificially self-contained.
work end bounded to PIC-12 for the commute matrix; home end bounded to PIC-12 for the reciprocal; peer comparison reads twelve states’ main files
Both ends are addresses on file. The home end is a residence record, not evidence anyone travelled.

sources.name: BLS Employment Projections, National Employment Matrix, industry to occupation
sources.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm
sources.is: The projection of which occupations an industry is made of, published as an industry-by-occupation matrix with a base year and a projected year.
sources.good: Saying what mix of jobs an industry runs on, and how that mix is expected to change over ten years.
sources.cannot: It is national only. No state or metro cut exists, so any regional headcount built from it is a synthetic estimate resting on an assumption that has to be stated in the same sentence as the number.
filters: 326000 plastics and rubber products manufacturing (325000, 326100, 326200 also fetched)
Line Item detailed occupations only; Summary rows excluded
NATIONAL ONLY: no state or metro cut exists; any regional count built from it is a synthetic estimate under a stated assumption, and the sentence says so

sources.name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, metropolitan file
sources.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm
sources.is: A survey of employers about which occupations they employ and what they pay, published as one snapshot a year for metropolitan areas.
sources.good: What a named occupation pays where the work is, against the same occupation nationally.
sources.cannot: One vintage is a level and never a trend: methods and area definitions change between years. Its top code is a ceiling rather than a value, and a starred or hashed cell is unknown, never zero.
filters: metropolitan area, carrying the same non-nesting caveat as BEA RPP
One year only. This is a level, not a trend; the wage trend on the talent page comes from QWI instead.

www.bls.gov returns 403 to a scripted request with no User-Agent and to one impersonating a browser, and 200 to one naming a contact address. contact.py holds the single address this repository sends. data.bls.gov, which the QCEW (the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages) pulls use, serves any of them.

sources.name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, national file
sources.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm
sources.is: The same survey’s national file, the benchmark half of the metro comparison.
sources.good: Giving a local wage something to be measured against that was collected the same way.
sources.cannot: It is all industries at once, so a national occupational wage is not the wage that occupation gets inside one industry. Some occupations appear as both a broad and a detailed row with identical values; keep one.
filters: the SOC (the Standard Occupational Classification, the federal job-title code) set read from oews.json (26 codes); the metro pull defines the set
51-2090 appears as broad and detailed with identical values; one row kept, detailed preferred
all industries; the ‘#’ ceiling ($115/hr, $239,200/yr) and ‘*’ are both null, never zero

sources.name: Census Quarterly Workforce Indicators, not seasonally adjusted
sources.terms: Public domain. The Census Bureau asks to be cited as the source of the original data: https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html
sources.is: A quarterly panel built from the same state employment records, following jobs rather than counting them once: hires, separations and the earnings of jobs that persist from one quarter to the next.
sources.good: How much hiring and separating sits behind a flat job count, and what a stable job pays.
sources.cannot: It restates its own history when the programme re-benchmarks, so a figure pulled today is not necessarily the figure published last year, and no archive of past vintages is fetched anywhere in this build. EarnBeg counts only workers who were already at the same employer the quarter before.
filters: 326 (plastics and rubber products manufacturing); 00 (all industries) as the benchmark on the talent demand chart
state 39, the twelve PIC-12 counties; and states 39, 17, 48, 06, 42, 18 and 26 published whole, for the churn page’s peer comparison
A00 (all ages) and A01 to A08, on the twelve PIC-12 counties, for the churn page’s age structure. agegrp is a PREDICATE: asking for it in `get=` returns HTTP 204 with an empty body

U (unadjusted), which is the API default and what every pull here uses. The `sa` in the path is the SEX-BY-AGE table, NOT seasonal adjustment; this registry called the series “seasonally adjusted” until 2026-09-01, when `seasonadj=U` was requested explicitly and returned identical values
EarnBeg is average monthly earnings of employees who also worked for the same employer in the prior quarter: stable jobs rather than new hires.

NOT keyless. A request without `key=` answers HTTP 200 with a web page titled “Missing Key”. HTTP 204 with an empty body is a real answer meaning no records, and is never a zero: Michigan returns 204 for every quarter from 2022Q1 at every industry.

sources.name: College Scorecard field-of-study earnings and debt, polymer engineering
sources.is: Federal earnings and debt figures for graduates of a named programme at a named institution.
sources.good: Attaching a real number to what a specific degree earned, from tax records rather than from a survey.
sources.cannot: It covers only students who took federal aid, so it is not all graduates. Its vintages differ by measure, so any ratio built across them mixes cohorts. And it reports what people who hold the degree earned, which is not what the occupation pays.
filters: latest = 2020 cohorts for 1-year earnings, 2022 file for 4-year earnings, 2019 file for debt; any ratio across them mixes cohorts
census_match=1 only - the Scorecard attaches Penn State Behrend’s values to Main Campus too, and the duplicate reads as a sixth institution
84% of cells are privacy-suppressed and suppression tracks program size; the five published institutions are the biggest programs, not a sample

derive_programs.py reads a held field-of-study tidy CSV filtered to census_match=1. This update reconciled that snapshot; it did not refresh the current Scorecard API. Rebuilding the display requires the held companion extract, which is not included as a raw file in this repository.

sources.name: USAspending award-level contract search
sources.terms: Public domain federal spending data. USAspending states no additional licence.
sources.is: The Treasury’s award-level record of federal contracting, queried for prime contracts only.
sources.good: Setting one award against everything the federal government contracts for in the same counties and years, on the same filter.
sources.cannot: It is filtered to prime contracts, so grants, loans and direct payments are deliberately outside it. Comparing a contract figure against all federal spending mixes those categories and was published here once, making the comparator twenty-six times too large. Place of performance is a filing field, not a statement about where work happened.
filters: POST with a JSON body; keyless. Filters: one spanning time_period 2018-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (FY2019-FY2026), place_of_performance_locations listing the 12 PIC-12 county codes, award_type_codes A-D (prime contracts; grants, loans and direct payments excluded), and naics_codes.

unlike the category endpoint, naics_codes IS sent to the API here, but it accepts only 2-, 4- or 6-digit codes: a 3-digit 325 returns 422 (‘only supported for lengths of 2, 4, and 6’). The pull sends the eleven 4-digit codes 3251-3259, 3261 and 3262, the same industry scope the category pull filters client-side.

The held 2026-08-31 award-register snapshot recorded 6,630 rows over 67 pages at limit 100, walked while page_metadata.hasNext. The original fetcher retains a 4,000-row probe floor and duplicate checks. This separately dated award-lifetime register was not refreshed with the 2026-09-08 transaction-category acquisition and cannot repair missing category pages.

Award Amount is the award’s WHOLE-LIFE obligation, not the slice inside the window: an award running since 2014 that the window touches carries every dollar since 2014. A different basis from the per-fiscal-year spending_by_category sums, and the two are never summed; the fed-award-basis-never-summed claim holds both surfaces to saying so.
place of performance, a reported field on the award rather than an observation of where work happened

Held 2026-08-31 award summaries, not the current fiscal-year flow and not a fresh acquisition in this update. Award Amount is whole-life obligations; do not add it to transaction-year totals or treat it as obligations inside the query window.

sources.name: USPTO Open Data Portal, patent applications search
sources.agency: United States Patent and Trademark Office
sources.terms: Public domain United States government work.
sources.is: The Patent Office’s live record of patent applications, searchable by classification code and by the addresses on the filing, roughly eighteen months after each application is filed.
sources.good: Whether a place still files inventions in a field: applications by filing year, cut by CPC class and by inventor or applicant address.
sources.cannot: It cannot see an application younger than the publication lag, so the newest years always look like a collapse and never are. An address is where the mail goes, not where the laboratory is: one Akron-assigned tire application carries a Luxembourg inventor, and the inventor and applicant bases differ by more than a factor of two. And an application is a filing, not a grant.
filters: POST with a JSON body carrying q and pagination; the count field of the reply is the figure, and no rows are read for a count.
applicationMetaData.cpcClassificationBag:C08*, organic macromolecular compounds. One defensible definition of polymer, and a choice.

inventor correspondence address (applicationMetaData.inventorBag.correspondenceAddressBag): geographicRegionCode for the state, countryCode for the nation, cityName for a city; swap inventorBag for applicantBag for the ownership basis, which gives 3,948 all-time against the inventor basis’s 8,854. The year filter is applicationMetaData.filingDate:[YYYY-01-01 TO YYYY-12-31], and the all-technology series is the same query with the CPC clause removed.

an application publishes about eighteen months after filing, so the newest filing years are undercounted by construction and always look like a collapse. Years after 2023 are flagged incomplete rather than dropped.

a genuine zero arrives as HTTP 404 whose body reads No matching records. The fetch accepts that as 0 only when the body says so; any other 404 fails loudly, because a failed request silently becoming a zero is the suppression trap one endpoint over.
PatentsView (search.patentsview.org) shut down 2026-03-20, and Patent Public Search answered every query with a 500 when tried on 2026-08-30. Both were candidate routes; neither is callable.

a count with NO country filter is worldwide filings at the USPTO and reads flat across a window in which American polymer filings fell 22 percent, because foreign-origin filings filled the hole. The first version of the patents page made exactly this error and a replication reviewer caught it before publication: filter countryCode or say you did not.

sources.name: GAC-PIC vault company records (catalogue)
sources.is: PIC’s own catalogue of companies it has classified. It is not public and a reader cannot obtain it.
sources.good: Describing a supply chain in more detail than any federal code can, using how companies describe themselves.
sources.cannot: It is a record of who PIC knows, not a census of who exists, so absence from it means only that PIC has not classified that company. Self-descriptions are quoted as written and never rewritten. It cannot be reproduced by anyone outside PIC, and any public release of the records themselves is gated on member consent.

NOT public and NOT reproducible by a reader. Company self-descriptions are quoted as written and are never rewritten: a company that writes ‘injection moulding’ said that. Any public release of these records is gated on member consent (Linear POL-1011).
The scoped offline repair reads the held SQLite extract and the previously published company fields. It is not a full catalogue rebuild or verification of current company capabilities.

contracting.invisible: Research grants are excluded by this view’s prime-contract award-type filter (A-D). Contract NAICS classifies the supplies or services acquired; a university’s identity does not determine that code. The view also filters to 325*/326* manufacturing codes and reported PIC-12 place of performance. An awardee address does not establish manufacturing activity in PIC-12. gaps.what: Twelve origin counties have no place name
gaps.why: The two local footprints are named and numbered on this page, but these origins are anywhere in the country and no NATIONAL county FIPS-to-name crosswalk ships in this repository, so those rows print a five-digit code a reader cannot use.
gaps.close: Add a national county crosswalk to the build. LEHD publishes a per-state geography crosswalk beside the LODES files, and the Census gazetteer is the other option; check that whichever is chosen covers out-of-state origins before wiring it in.

gaps.what: The award register is a separately dated snapshot
gaps.why: The category totals were refreshed on 8 September 2026. The separate recipient register is a 31 August snapshot whose original raw response is unavailable; it is not a reconciliation of the refreshed totals.
gaps.close: Refresh the award-level records with preserved raw responses and reconcile fiscal-year transactions before assigning the peaks to recipients.

gaps.what: No archive of past QWI releases
gaps.why: The programme restates whole histories when it re-benchmarks, and nothing in this build fetches an earlier vintage, so how far those restatements move a published number is unmeasured here.
gaps.close: One stored file per historical release. The live API serves only the latest recomputation, so this has to be collected going forward.

gaps.what: One derivation step is missing from the build
gaps.why: The step that turns the fetched price series into that page’s shipped file is not present in _data/build/, so the page’s data is a frozen derived artifact rather than a reproducible one.
gaps.close: Restore the derivation script, and have it emit the meta prose the page’s methodology box renders.

gaps.what: Some pages name a rebuild script that is not in this repository
gaps.why: The page READMEs that name build_db.py, fetch_control_cips.py tell a reader to run a file _data/build/ does not contain, so those pages ship a derived artifact that cannot be regenerated from this clone. The fetch scripts behind them are all present; it is the derivation step that is absent. Named here because a rebuild command that fails is worse than none: it reads as reproducibility.
gaps.close: Ship the derivation scripts, or change those READMEs to say the shipped file is the artifact, the way the two internal registers in the register above already do.

gaps.why: The earlier C1746 metro discloses every year from 2015 through 2023. The C1741 metro adds Ashtabula in 2024. A missing line under the newer code was wrongly described as withheld data; it is a geography break.
gaps.close: The peers page now shows the earlier disclosed history separately. A continuous comparison needs a constant-boundary county aggregation; do not splice the two metro definitions.
